prompt: You have $40$ meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular garden. What is the largest area, in square meters, you can enclose?
hint: Call the width $x$. Then the length is $20 - x$ (half the fence goes to one width plus one length). Write the area as a function of $x$.

hints.text: Call the width $x$. Then the length is $20 - x$ (half the fence goes to one width plus one length). Write the area as a function of $x$.
$x = 10$, so the garden is $10 \times 10$ and the area is $100$ m².

explanation: Constraint: $2x + 2y = 40$, so $y = 20 - x$. Area: $A(x) = x(20 - x) = 20x - x^2$.
$A'(x) = 20 - 2x = 0$ gives $x = 10$. Since $A'' = -2 < 0$, this is a maximum.

alternativeExplanations.title: Try some rectangles
steps: The area peaks when the sides are equal.
For a fixed perimeter, the square always wins — calculus just proves what the table suggests.
